answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money; 1 active association worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers below it; draws 8 Zoo cards and keeps 4; draws 2 Final Scoring cards; places Animals side I in the leftmost Action slot (strength 1), with the other four side-I cards randomly in the remaining slots. Appeal starts staggered by turn order: 0 for the start player, then 1, 2, and 3 for second, third, and fourth.
answers.evidence: Personal setup: ‘Place one card side I up under each ... Animals card under the leftmost slot’; ‘Place your appeal ... counters ... start player on space 0 ... fourth on space 3’; ‘Take 25 money’; ‘Draw 2 Final Scoring cards’; ‘Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4’.

answers.answer: At setup, four Base Conservation Project cards are face up below the Association board in a four-player game; three are face up in games with fewer players. In a two-player game, unused-color tokens block the left level on the left project, middle level on the middle project, right level on the right project, and the three spaces in the donation area's left column. No such blocking is specified for three- or four-player games. The initial six-card display is revealed only after everyone has chosen starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c: ‘In a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up ... otherwise the 3 topmost’; ‘2-player game only’ blocks the listed levels and donation spaces. Personal setup G: ‘After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.’

answers.answer: After using the card in slot 4, move it to slot 1; shift the cards that were in slots 1–3 one slot right. Set action strength before performing the action. Each X-token spent adds 1 strength and returns to supply; any number may be spent, but strength above 5 may not help some actions. You can hold at most 5 X-tokens, and tokens gained during an action cannot boost that same action. Resolve an ‘after finishing’ effect only after the action is complete and the used Action card has moved.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘shift all Action cards left of the now-empty slot one slot to the right’; X-tokens: ‘each token spent adds +1 strength’ and ‘You can never hold more than 5’; ‘set the strength before performing’; After finishing effects occur after completing the action, ‘including moving the Action cards’.

answers.answer: You may not take a regular action that does nothing (such as playing zero animals or building zero buildings). If you cannot or do not want to perform one of the five actions, select an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token instead. Move that card to slot 1 and shift the intervening cards right; slot strength and upgrade side do not matter. You cannot take this action while holding 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘You may not do nothing’. X-token action: ‘take exactly 1 X-token’; ‘select an Action card, move it to slot 1, and shift the intervening cards right’; ‘If you already have 5 X-tokens, you cannot perform this action.’

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, the break happens after the triggering player's current turn. That player gains 1 X-token for reaching the last space; any extra movement beyond the last space is ignored. The player finishes the current turn, then everyone completes the break procedure. After the break the token returns to the player-count starting space and play continues clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: Break track: ‘break takes place after the end of your current turn’ and ‘you get 1 X-token’; ‘Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space.’ After a break, ‘the token returns to its starting space’; break step 6: ‘Play then continues clockwise with the next player.’

answers.answer: Cards I always advances the Break token 2 spaces, then either draws from the deck or, at strength 5+, snaps exactly 1 display card of any reputation instead of drawing. Side-I draw/discard by strength 1/2/3/4/5+ is 1/1, 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1 cards. Cards II also advances the Break token 2 spaces, then draws from the deck and/or from the display within reputation range, in any order; side-II draw/discard at strength 1/2/3/4/5+ is 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1, 4/1. Its snap threshold is strength 3 and a snap is exactly 1 display card of any reputation with no deck draw. The reputation restriction applies to the side-II display draw, not to snapping. Display cards taken during a turn are replenished only after the turn is complete. Hand size is unlimited during play and enforced at breaks.
answers.evidence: Cards action: side I ‘Advance the Break token 2 spaces’ and strength 5 snap; side II advances 2, draws from deck and/or in-range display, and snap works from strength 3. It says snapping takes ‘exactly one display card of any reputation’; display is not replenished until turn complete. Hand limit: ‘There is no in-turn hand limit; you only discard to your limit during breaks.’

answers.answer: ‘Within reputation range’ means the display card in the folder matching your Reputation counter and all lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action (Cards II). Beyond reputation 15, the counter stays at 15 and each remaining reputation step gives 1 appeal. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display: ‘Within reputation range’ is the matching folder plus lower-numbered folders; ‘Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action’; on space 15, further reputation gives ‘1 appeal per remaining reputation step’; ‘You may not look through the discard pile’.

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building of your choice up to the action strength; pay 2 money per space before placing it. Build II may build any number of different buildings whose combined size is no greater than action strength, but not two identical buildings in that action; each is paid for separately at 2 money per space. The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building along at least one edge. Build only on empty spaces and do not cover water or rock; restricted-icon spaces require Build II. Every new kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately increases appeal by 1, once per pavilion.
answers.evidence: Build I: ‘Build exactly 1 building ... of size up to the action's strength’ and ‘Pay 2 money per space’. Placement rules specify first building on a border, later adjacency, empty spaces, restricted spaces requiring upgraded Build, and kiosk spacing. Pavilion: ‘immediately (and only once) increases your zoo's appeal by 1.’

answers.answer: Build I can build standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), kiosks, pavilions, and one Petting Zoo per zoo (size 3). Build II additionally allows Reptile Houses and Large Bird Aviaries (size 5 each); it can build multiple different buildings in one action, with total size no greater than strength and no identical buildings in that action. The supply has four tiles of each special enclosure type, while an individual zoo may have only one of each type. Unique buildings cannot be built with the Build action and enter through Sponsor cards. When all map spaces except water and rock are covered, gain 7 appeal immediately; reaching restricted-icon spaces requires Build II, though the complete-coverage effect can also result from other effects.
answers.evidence: Buildings table and Build rules list the I/II buildings and limits; ‘The supply has four tiles of each special enclosure’; ‘Unique buildings can never be built with this action’; Build II full-map rule grants ‘7 appeal’ when every space except water and rock is covered.

answers.answer: Yes. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards, and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action. Resolve items one at a time, and pay each item before receiving its own benefits. Immediate effects resolve as their triggering event occurs; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the entire action is complete and the Action card has moved. If effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: X-tokens/turn principles: ‘Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps’; ‘You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits.’ Animal play effects distinguish immediate from after-finishing effects; simultaneous effects: ‘you choose the order.’

answers.answer: For each animal, check and meet all card conditions, pay its cost, house it, place its card, and resolve its effects. A partner zoo on the animal's continent discounts the cost by 3 money for each continent icon on that animal card, so a double icon gets a 6-money discount. A non-Petting-Zoo animal may use an empty standard enclosure at least its required size; flip that enclosure to occupied. Petting Zoo animals must use the Petting Zoo. All reptiles and some birds may instead use their special enclosure if its required spaces are free; place the indicated number of your tokens on it, and never flip a special enclosure. Required water/rock adjacency applies to the chosen enclosure; count distinct adjacent terrain hexes, not multiple touching edges to one hex. Effects such as appeal, conservation, and reputation resolve after placement; ordinary effects are immediate, while ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the entire Animals action and card movement are complete. Pay the animal before receiving its own benefits.
answers.evidence: Animals action steps require conditions, cost, empty enclosure, card placement, then effects; partner zoo discount is ‘3 money per continent icon’. The enclosure table says standard enclosures flip occupied and special enclosures take player tokens and ‘never flip’. Animal rules specify distinct adjacent water/rock hexes and after-finishing timing.

answers.answer: Animals II permits animals from the display within your reputation range, with an additional cost equal to the folder number. At strength 5 or more, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, so your range is already higher for that action. Display cards are not replenished until the turn ends. Animals II also allows animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon. The side-II animal capacity is 1/1/2/2/2 at strengths 1/2/3/4/5+.
answers.evidence: Animals II: display animals within range with ‘additional cost equal to the folder number’; at strength 5+, reputation increases ‘at the very beginning’; display is not replenished until turn end; may play upgrade-required animals. Capacity table gives side-II 1/1/2/2/2.

answers.answer: Existing animals may move into a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary only immediately when that building is built, and only once per building. You may move all suitable animals that fit, choosing separately for each; mark the animal's indicated number of special-enclosure spaces with player tokens. If an animal could live in a special enclosure, remove its indicated special-enclosure tokens if possible; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements (including water/rock). If none meets all requirements, use the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size; if none meets even the size, flip none.
answers.evidence: Build II: when building either enclosure, ‘immediately ... move all suitable animals that fit’. Special enclosures are marked with the number of spaces shown using player tokens. Moving-animals edge case gives the one-time timing and smallest-enclosure/fallback procedure.

answers.answer: Association task strengths are: increase reputation 2, gain partner zoo 3, gain university 4, and conservation project work 5. Association I performs exactly one task; it needs at least one active worker. A task normally takes one worker, but if one of yours is already on that task, the next use requires two workers; if three of yours are there, you cannot repeat it before the break. Other players' workers on the task do not matter. Association II can perform one or more different tasks, with total task value at most the action strength, using one or two of your workers per task under the same repeat rule; it may also make one donation, but only after at least one task in that action.
answers.evidence: Association I lists task strengths 2/3/4/5 and says exactly one task; worker repetition: use 2 if one is already there and cannot if 3 are there; ‘Other players' workers ... do not matter.’ Side II permits different tasks with total value no greater than strength and max one donation after a task.

answers.answer: Take partner zoos and universities from the available tiles on the Association board and place each on the lowest empty matching space on your zoo map; take any printed space bonus immediately. Partner zoos must be from different continents, with at most four total; the third (and fourth) requires Association II. A university cannot duplicate one you already have. Partner zoos provide their continent icon and reduce animal costs from that continent by 3 money per matching continent icon. Universities provide research icons and reputation as printed; they are the only way to raise the hand limit to 5, and only the university with that printed benefit does so.
answers.evidence: Association tasks say tiles move from the board to the lowest empty map space with printed bonuses; partners must be different continents, max 4, and third/fourth need upgraded Association. Universities cannot be duplicates; they grant reputation/research, and are the only way to increase hand limit to 5. FAQ confirms tile bonuses use an available Association-board tile.

answers.answer: Association project work can support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project from hand and support it immediately; Association II can also play one from the in-range display, paying its folder number. A new card enters above the Association board in the leftmost space, pushing cards right; the limit is 2, 3, or 4 cards depending on player count. If it exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost project and return tokens on it to their owners' supplies. To support, fulfill an unoccupied condition and put one of your player tokens from the left edge of your zoo map on it. A reward level can hold only one token total across players, and normally you may support a particular project only once. Removing the map token activates its bonus immediately; you choose whether to take that bonus before or after the project reward. Base projects below the board stay in place. Tokens on an overflowing discarded project return to supply, not to the map; its already activated map bonus remains activated.
answers.evidence: Conservation project work describes supporting an existing or newly played card; Association II allows display play for folder cost. The support rules specify unoccupied levels, one token per level across players, once per project, token source, and bonus timing. Overflow rule returns tokens to supply; base projects are never moved.

answers.answer: A release project's printed standard-enclosure category must match the animal's printed standard requirement: 2− accepts size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5; actual enclosure tile size or special-enclosure capacity does not set the category. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, then discard it, losing its icons. Keep its previously gained conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play grants none. To free its space, if it can live in a special enclosure remove its required tokens if possible; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, or fall back to the smallest occupied enclosure meeting size alone; if none meets size, flip none.
answers.evidence: Release rules give the size categories and state tile/capacity do not define them. They say ‘First lose only the animal's printed appeal’, discard its icons, and keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and prior effects. New-card play grants 1 reputation; support of one already in play does not. The enclosure fallback is specified in the release procedure.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly one Sponsor from hand, with action strength at least its level and all conditions met; resolve its instant/triggered effects and then place it. Alternatively, advance the Break token by the action strength and take that amount of money, even if fewer steps remain before the final space. Sponsors II may play one or more cards from hand or from the in-range display (pay the folder number for each); action strength plus 1 must cover their combined levels, and X-tokens can raise strength above 5. Resolve multiple cards one after another, finishing each card's immediate effects before the next, except after-finishing effects. Display replenishment waits until turn end. If using the break-money option on side II, take the money twice (twice the action strength), including when movement reaches the last space early.
answers.evidence: Sponsors I money option says take strength money ‘even if the Break token doesn't need all the steps’. Side II adds money twice; level budget is strength +1, and display cards cost folder number with no refill until turn end. Multiple cards resolve one after another, with after-finishing effects deferred.

answers.answer: Break order: discard to hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with the particular university); clear Multiplier, Venom, and Constriction tokens from Action cards; return workers and replenish available partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, slide remaining cards down, and refill; take income; reset the Break token. Income includes appeal-track money, kiosk income, and break-income Sponsor/map bonuses. Each kiosk pays 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, and pavilion. Empty standard enclosures do not count, while empty special enclosures do. If multiple players take display cards during break income, resolve them clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them) and refill the display after each such player's income, before the next affected player chooses.
answers.support: Break procedure lists the ordered steps and hand limits. Kiosk income lists qualifying neighbors and excludes empty standard enclosures while including empty special enclosures. The income paragraph specifies clockwise order and refill after each display-card-taking player's income.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation points, choose either an Action-card upgrade or activate an additional association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or the Bonus token by that space (if available). The first time anyone reaches 10, all players discard one Final Scoring card; if nobody reaches 10 before game end, all discard one before final scoring. The end is checked at the end of your own turn or during a break: it triggers when your Appeal and Conservation counters enter the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits until the end of your own turn or a break to trigger, unless another player triggers the end first. If triggered at the end of a player's turn, that player finishes and every other player takes one more turn; if triggered during a break, all players take one more turn. Each Final Scoring card can grant at most 4 conservation points. Victory Points equal your Appeal value minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive score wins; ties go to the player with the most supported conservation projects, then tied players share the victory.
answers.evidence: Conservation milestones specify rewards at 2, 5, 8, and 10 and the no-10 fallback. End-of-game text gives trigger checks, delayed appeal timing, and final turns. Final scoring states the 4-point cap, VP formula, positive-score winner, and support-count tiebreak/shared victory.
